events.title: Maximilien Robespierre is born
events.description: The future French revolutionary leader was born on this day in Arras, France. He trained as a lawyer before rising to prominence during the French Revolution.
events.significance: Robespierre became one of the most influential and controversial figures of the Revolution, and his name is closely linked with the Reign of Terror.

events.title: Sigmund Freud is born
events.description: The Austrian neurologist who would found psychoanalysis was born on this day. His ideas about the unconscious mind changed how people think about human behavior.
events.significance: Freud's theories shaped psychology, medicine, literature, and popular culture, and they are still debated today.

events.title: Henry David Thoreau dies
events.description: The American essayist and philosopher died on this day at age 44. He is best remembered for 'Walden' and his essay on civil disobedience.
events.significance: Thoreau's writings on nature, simplicity, and peaceful resistance influenced later movements for environmentalism and civil rights.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower opens to the public
events.description: The wrought-iron tower officially opened at the Universal Exposition in Paris. It was built as the entrance to the world's fair and was the tallest structure in the world at the time.
events.significance: Once criticized by some Parisians, the tower became the enduring symbol of France and one of the most visited monuments in the world.

events.title: The Hindenburg disaster
events.description: The German airship Hindenburg caught fire and was destroyed within about a minute while trying to dock at Lakehurst, New Jersey. Thirty-six people died.
events.significance: The filmed and broadcast disaster shattered public confidence in passenger airships and effectively ended the era of commercial zeppelin travel.
